In the episode, we talk about the benefits of writing poetry, why I enjoy reading translated poets, and other esoteric topics.

For today’s prompt, write an ordinary object poem. The poem could be about the ordinary object, or it could mention an ordinary object in passing. The more specific the better, I think. Like a fine blue Pilot G-2 pen or an old pair of Nike Quest 6 running shoes. Perhaps a Bulbasaur Pez Dispenser. Not that any of these specific ordinary objects are in my desk area at this moment. Well, maybe.
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at an Ordinary Object Poem:

It’s easy to say something
bad could happen; bad things
happen every day. Just by
the simple act of sitting down
and standing up, a small tear
turns into a hole in the rear
of my thrift store blue jeans.
Maybe it’s a bit dramatic
to say everything can go
wrong, can fall apart, and
reveal too much skin; then
again, I loved those jeans,
and it’s not likely I’ll find
another perfect pair, so
let me plunge headfirst
into my fashion despair
in a Walmart world that
likely wouldn’t even care
about my denim reason
when flannel’s in season
and thrifting is treason.
Humor me: These jeans
meant a nice fit for me,
a relaxed look you see,
that also helped me be
a more confident he
in a sad cargo khaki sea
of pants made for me.
